scope: Fresh source identity/text-layer inspection plus read-only inventory of existing structured transcription and independent review records. This is not a fresh transcription or rendered-fidelity approval.

coverage.note: Counts describe actual JSON, not correctness. Page 6 has only three rows; page 7 resumes at 2:31. Data are not a contiguous complete Quran. Page 1 contains all seven Fatihah body verses but source ornamental title and rendered character anchoring remain unverified.

unresolved.evidence_needed: The same glyph checked on other alif-lam-meem openings in this edition (PDF pages for 3:1, 29:1, 30:1, 31:1, 32:1). The glyph was matched shape for shape against known shaddas on this same page (muttaqin, allazina, as-salata, mimma), so its identity as a shadda is not in doubt - only its meaning is.

unresolved.question: The two signs inside 2:2 (after rayba and after fiihi) are printed as three dots in a triangle over a short stroke, stacked above a dotted jeem. Is this one composite waqf sign of this edition, or the mu'anaqah three dots printed together with a separate jeem? It is transcribed as U+06DB followed by jeem.
unresolved.evidence_needed: This edition's own waqf-sign key, if it prints one (the verified footer legend on PDF pages 4 and 5 covers only the tinted band letters, not the in-line waqf marks). Failing that, a sweep for a bare three-dot mark with no jeem, and for a jeem with no dots, elsewhere in the volume.

unresolved.question: PDF page 2 prints no folio number anywhere - not in the head, foot or side margins. Should printed_page stay null, or should the renderer show the number the neighbouring pages imply?
unresolved.evidence_needed: A product decision, not a source question. The source fact is settled: PDF page 4 prints ৫ and PDF page 5 prints ৬, both centred in the footer legend strip, so the offset is PDF n -> printed n+1 and PDF 2 WOULD be ৩. But page 2 is a surah-opening page: it has the full ornamental frame and no footer legend strip, and it carries no number. ৩ is an inference from neighbours, not something this page prints, so printed_page is null. Independently corroborated: the Arabic agent reached the same conclusion for this page (its U2-NO-FOLIO, printed_page null).

unresolved.question: Is the space before each danda U+0964 an encoded space in the original text, or only printed letterspacing?
unresolved.evidence_needed: The publisher's source file. A scan cannot establish ENCODED whitespace. What is measured: every danda on page 2 is preceded by a visible gap of 44-52 px at 600 dpi (r0 'মীম ।' 52 px, r1 'হিদায়াত ।' 44 px, r2 'করে ।' 49 px, r4 'হয়েছে ।' 52 px and 'রাখে ।' 48 px), against ordinary inter-word gaps of 34-58 px on the same lines. The gap is therefore indistinguishable in width from a normal word space. It is transcribed as a single space before the danda; the terminator is the Bengali danda U+0964, never an ASCII period.

unresolved.question: Do this agent's rNwM word ids and word widths line up with the Arabic agent's? Largely settled; two boundaries remain soft.
unresolved.evidence_needed: Reconciled against page-002/arabic/arabic.json after that file landed. The id scheme agrees exactly: same word count per row, same right-to-left numbering, and لَا / رَيْبَ split as two words (r0w4 / r0w5) by both agents independently. Every one of the 48 sign centres falls inside the word box its target names under the Arabic agent's segmentation, so NO target changed. offset_in_word is now computed against that file's word edges, because that is what the renderer positions against. Comparing the two independent measurements: 44 of 48 offsets agreed within 0.02 before reconciliation. The four that moved further - r2-a11 -0.033, r2-a12 -0.038, r4-a5 -0.042, and r2-a10 -0.020 - all sit on the two word boundaries that BOTH agents independently flagged as falling inside a continuous ink run (رَزَقْنٰهُمْ / يُنْفِقُوْنَ and هُمْ / يُوْقِنُوْنَ); see the Arabic agent's U2-WORD-SPLIT-INK-RUN and U-LA-RAYB here. If agent 3 moves either boundary, those offsets must be recomputed - the sign x positions are measured and do not change.

unresolved.question: In row 0, are لَا and رَيْبَ set as two words or one? This decides whether r0w4/r0w5 exist as recorded.
unresolved.evidence_needed: The Arabic agent's segmentation. Measured: the gap between them is 22 px, against 30-70 px at every other word boundary in that row and 11-18 px inside words - so it sits between the two populations. They are recorded here as two words because that is the orthographic split. If they are one word, r0-a6 (১) through r0-a10 (oval wedge) all belong to that one word and their offsets change.

unresolved.question: Is the ringed sign at row 0, x 2316-2386 a ringed ২, and therefore the conditional দম ফেলিলে দুই আলিফ?
unresolved.evidence_needed: A higher-resolution scan, or a second instance elsewhere in the book to cross-check. It was matched side by side against the ringed ২ printed in this edition's own page-5 legend and against the ringed ১ in the neighbouring cell; it is not the ১. It is the only ringed digit on page 2. It is recorded as conditional, which is the safe direction: the project's worst recorded error is turning a conditional rule into an absolute one.

unresolved.question: Is the 12 px mark in band 4 at x 1629-1641 a printed sign or scanner dirt?
unresolved.evidence_needed: A cleaner scan of the same page. At 12 px it is about a quarter the width of every real sign on this page (48-79 px) and resolves into two unconnected specks with no glyph structure. It is excluded from the glyph list as dirt. If it is ink, band 4 has ten signs, not nine.

unresolved.question: Per-word sibilant and nukta calls in the Bengali that a 297 ppi scan cannot settle at high confidence.
unresolved.evidence_needed: A higher-resolution scan, or the publisher's text. Word by word, as read: 'সেই', 'সন্দেহ', 'সালাত' are read as স (the initial has the open left curl and internal diagonal of স, not the flag of শ or the closed bowl of ষ) - medium-to-high, NOT certain. NOTE that no ষ্ট or ষ্ঠ conjunct occurs anywhere on page 2, so the ষ্ট/ষ্ঠ ambiguity that the project warns about does not arise on this page. On nukta: 'রিযিক' and 'নাযিল' are read as bare য with NO nukta dot; 'গায়েবের', 'কায়েম', 'হয়েছে', 'ব্যয়', 'ইয়াকীন' and 'দিয়েছি' are read as য় WITH the nukta. At this floor a printed nukta and a scan speckle are the same size, so each nukta call is medium, not certain. 'কোন' and 'সন্দেহ' are read with ন, not ণ; the ন্দ conjunct in সন্দেহ is legible and is not ণ্ড.
